name: SimplePractice Telehealth
description: Telehealth by SimplePractice is the video-appointment feature integrated into SimplePractice's electronic health record and practice-management platform for therapists and other health and wellness practitioners.
agentUseSummary: SimplePractice Telehealth is not a separate installable API authority. It is an integrated SimplePractice product feature, and SimplePractice explicitly states that it does not offer a public-facing API for integrations with other software or platforms. Relay therefore keeps the unavailable authority under the canonical SimplePractice provider rather than duplicating connection state or collecting portal and meeting credentials.

blocked.description: Telehealth is an integrated SimplePractice feature and does not publish a separate OAuth, API-key or remote MCP connection contract.

blocked.label: Collect portal or meeting credentials
blocked.description: Relay does not collect SimplePractice usernames, passwords, MFA codes, session cookies, client-portal credentials or private appointment links.

blocked.label: Use private Telehealth interfaces
blocked.description: Relay does not scrape appointment links, reverse engineer private meeting traffic or access video, audio, chat, captions, transcripts, notes or session summaries through undocumented interfaces.

blocked.label: Automate Telehealth workflows
blocked.description: Relay does not automate clinician or client portals, waiting rooms, calls, recordings, reminders, appointments or clinical workflows through a browser.

blocked.label: Create duplicate SimplePractice connection state
blocked.description: Any future supported account API belongs once under the canonical SimplePractice provider, not under this product-feature identity.

approvalProfiles.description: No action is exposed under the Telehealth feature identity; SimplePractice publishes no supported direct account API, and any future developer authority belongs to the canonical SimplePractice provider.

SimplePractice Telehealth is not a standalone API authority, so Relay mounts no portal, meeting, media or browser tools in Hermes.

providerSetup.blocker: SimplePractice describes Telehealth as a feature fully integrated with its EHR, calendar, client details, reminders, billing, claims and Client Portal. Clinicians and clients launch product-controlled appointments through the SimplePractice web or mobile applications and private appointment links. SimplePractice explicitly states that it does not currently offer a public-facing API for integrations with other software or platforms. Telehealth therefore has no independent developer application, delegated authorization contract, supported endpoints, schemas, scopes, rate limits, webhooks or revocation lifecycle. Treating meeting links or portal access as an API would duplicate the canonical SimplePractice identity and create unsafe access to protected clinical communications and session media.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request SimplePractice or Telehealth credentials, meeting links or media access, and do not show Connect. Reconsider only if SimplePractice publishes a supported distributable account API, delegated OAuth contract, API-key contract or remote MCP service with appropriate healthcare-data and telehealth-media terms; implement that authority once under the canonical SimplePractice provider.

evidence.supports: SimplePractice's current feature-plan FAQ says Telehealth is an integrated subscription feature and explicitly states that SimplePractice does not offer a public-facing API for integrations with other software or platforms.

SimplePractice describes Telehealth as integrated with its practice-management tools, video appointments, calendar, client details, reminders, billing, claims and Client Portal rather than as a separate developer platform.
SimplePractice markets Telehealth as a HIPAA-compliant feature launched directly from its calendar with product-generated appointment links, waiting room, chat, screen sharing and whiteboard.
The official mobile workflow uses SimplePractice's clinician, client-portal and Telehealth apps plus private appointment links; it does not document a third-party application interface.
SimplePractice documents sensitive in-session controls for participant access, waiting rooms, chat, captions, screen sharing and related media entirely inside the product UI.
SimplePractice documents optional audio transcription and draft clinical-note workflows within Telehealth, reinforcing that undocumented automation could expose highly sensitive session content.
